title: One-layer reduction of the integer stalk bound
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space whose quasi-compact opens are closed under pairwise intersection, and let $\iota:K\to C$ be a monomorphism of abelian sheaves with $C\simeq\underline{\mathbf Z}_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Assume $K$ receives an epimorphism from a finite sum of extensions by zero of constant integer sheaves on quasi-compact opens [def-sc-abelian-open-extension-by-zero]. Fix group isomorphisms $e_x:C_x\simeq\mathbf Z$ for every $x$, and $b\in\mathbf N$, such that each image of $e_x\iota_x$ is $a\mathbf Z$ for some $0\le a\le b+1$. Stalks are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Then there is a monomorphism $l:L\to K$ with L also generated by finitely many such compact-open sections, and every image of $e_x\iota_x l_x$ is $a\mathbf Z$ with $0\le a\le b$. There are quasi-compact opens $V\subseteq U$ and a short exact complex [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] whose first, second and third objects are respectively isomorphic to $j_{V!}\underline{\mathbf Z}_V$, $j_{U!}\underline{\mathbf Z}_U$, and $\operatorname{coker}(l)$.

source.place: Lemma 0A38 (cohomology-lemma-subsheaf-of-constant-sheaf), first paragraph and filtration/final paragraphs

proof.text: Apply the lower-layer generator construction to obtain L,l, finite generation, its bound b, compact V⊆U, and q:j_U!Z→coker l. Its quotient stalk vanishes on V and off U; q is a stalk isomorphism on U minus V.

Take f:j_V!Z→j_U!Z from the nested-open inclusion theorem. Extension stalks vanish outside their open. Thus f followed by q vanishes on every stalk: the target is zero on V, and the source is zero off V. Equality of sheaf morphisms is detected on stalks by section_ext, so f≫q=0. Form S=ShortComplex.mk f q.

On V, f is a stalk isomorphism and the quotient stalk is zero. On U minus V, the first stalk is zero and q is a stalk isomorphism. Outside U all three stalks are zero. In the first case use ShortComplex.exact_iff_epi, in the second exact_iff_mono, and in the third exact_of_isZero_X₂. The zero-object mono and epi criteria provide the endpoint conditions. Apply the abelian-sheaf stalkwise short-exactness criterion. All three objects of S are literally the desired objects, so the concluding isomorphisms are Iso.refl.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 0A38; the first two steps are split into the lower-layer generator lemma, and the nested-open inclusion is separated from the stalkwise exactness argument. Lean assembly written by A2.
